A parameter of a route may name a **converter**, the `int` of `<int:room>`, which supplies the regular expression for that part of the path and turns the text it matches into a value; a parameter that names none gets `str` ([Routes, regular expressions and converters](urls/patterns.md)) (`django/urls/resolvers.py:RoutePattern`, `django/urls/resolvers.py:RegexPattern`, `django/urls/converters.py:IntConverter`).

Importing the module runs the calls that build everything under the root ([From a URLconf to a tree](urls/urlconf.md), [When a URLconf is imported](urls/import.md)) (`django/urls/resolvers.py:_get_cached_resolver`, `django/urls/resolvers.py:URLResolver.urlconf_module`).

At the centre of the middleware chain, `BaseHandler._get_response`, or its asynchronous twin, calls `BaseHandler.resolve_request`, which asks `get_resolver` for the root resolver and calls `URLResolver.resolve` on it with the request's `path_info` (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler.resolve_request`).

`resolve_request` keeps the last as `HttpRequest.resolver_match`, and the handler calls the view with the arguments in it (`django/urls/resolvers.py:URLResolver.resolve`, `django/urls/resolvers.py:URLPattern.resolve`).

`resolve_request` keeps the last as `HttpRequest.resolver_match`, and the handler calls the view with the arguments in it (`django/urls/resolvers.py:URLResolver.resolve`, `django/urls/resolvers.py:URLPattern.resolve`).

The candidates under an include without a namespace are lifted into the table above it, with the include's route in front; a resolver with an application namespace keeps a table of its own, and `reverse` goes from namespace to namespace before it looks the name up ([Reversing a name](urls/reversing.md), [`normalize`, and the patterns that cannot be reversed](urls/normalize.md), [Namespaces](urls/namespaces.md)) (`django/urls/resolvers.py:URLResolver._populate`, `django/utils/regex_helper.py:normalize`).

If every candidate is tried and none passes, it raises `NoReverseMatch` (`django/urls/base.py:reverse`, `django/urls/resolvers.py:URLResolver._reverse_with_prefix`).
If every candidate is tried and none passes, it raises `NoReverseMatch` (`django/urls/base.py:reverse`, `django/urls/resolvers.py:URLResolver._reverse_with_prefix`).

So a route with parameters is kept twice over: as a regular expression to resolve with, which `_route_to_regex` makes of the route as the URLconf is imported, and as a string to reverse with, which `normalize` makes of that expression; and each of its converters works in both directions (`django/urls/resolvers.py:_route_to_regex`).

A middleware that sets an attribute named `"urlconf"` on the request gives it a URLconf of its own, which becomes the current one when the request is resolved ([The script prefix, the current URLconf and the caches](urls/state.md)) (`django/urls/resolvers.py:_get_cached_resolver`, `django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler.get_response`).
